source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor get 'STATUS_FAN 1~N' 2>&1; echo ---SDR-FALLBACK---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -100
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns FULL raw `ipmitool (OOB lanplus) sensor get "<SENSOR>"` reading + threshold; user judges (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES treats the symbolic `1~N` expression as one sensor, so it cannot discover N, prove full fan population coverage or interpret vendor-specific discrete status bits. It also assumes a status sensor necessarily has numeric thresholds and truncates discovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires discovery-first enumeration, state decoding and read-only evidence. V3.1 additionally binds every channel to fan module, rotor, controller/header and redundancy zone, separates presence/status from RPM and thermal thresholds, and records explicitly which fields are not applicable.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 903/2291 accepts the literal expression and reports no risk, leaving N, channel identity, discrete event masks, UI parity, freshness and absence semantics unaudited.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Wistron-BMC-00088-V004 is a separate physical removal/insertion case with unresolved `1~N` versus `1~16` and temperature-versus-status contradictions; it remains ENGINEER DECISION PENDING and supplies no authority to set N or remove fans here. RPM/temperature cases are distinct coverage.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1065, Wistron-BMC-00194-V004 or fcc4729918b0d0c0 draft exists in the invalidated run; its related dynamic fan-status record is not this case.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this passive Sensor Page variant.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves `STATUS_FAN 1~N`; ED-34 treats N, topology and state specification as Project readiness; ED-35 prohibits fan removal, PWM change or airflow obstruction; ED-38 preserves logs, forbids automatic retry and keeps the verdict engineer-owned. The unresolved dynamic-row decision cannot be silently imported.

original_test_intent: Verify every Project-installed fan status channel represented by `STATUS_FAN 1~N` is present and correctly rendered in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, with N determined from approved platform inventory and each discrete state mapped to the correct fan/rotor/controller location and vendor definition.
original_method: Discover the authoritative fitted fan/rotor population and stable status records, query every exact channel through the supported BMC path, and correlate raw discrete state, event masks and freshness with the unchanged UI. Compare only applicable status fields to Project SPEC; do not invent numeric thresholds or stimulate a fault.
manual_activity: The thermal/platform owner confirms the fitted fan-module and rotor count N, maps each status channel to hardware and supplies the discrete-state contract. Automation can enumerate and collect passive BMC/UI state. A human resolves any optional or redundant position and owns the verdict; no physical fan action is authorized.
required_inputs: Chassis/fan-board PN/revision, BMC/SDR build and approved fitted fan-module/rotor inventory defining N
Per-channel fan module, rotor, slot, controller/header, zone and redundancy-group mapping
Stable SDR/API/UI identity, sensor/event reading types, raw assertion/deassertion masks and display-string mapping
Definition of presence, normal, degraded, failed/stalled, absent, redundancy-lost, unavailable, stale and initializing states
Applicability of thresholds for a discrete status record and separate RPM/tach/temperature sensor references
Polling/UI propagation/freshness tolerance and current fan policy/mode
Protected ipmitool/API/browser access and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or approved manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, fan, thermal or BMC logs; existing status transitions are relevant evidence.
Do not send `sensor get 'STATUS_FAN 1~N'`. Resolve N and enumerate each exact status record from the approved inventory and full SDR data.
Do not assume N is 16 from the conflicting dynamic case, count rotors as modules, or silently omit optional/fitted fans.
Do not interpret a discrete status record as RPM or temperature and do not require numeric thresholds when the sensor definition marks them not applicable.

Do not stop/remove/reseat a fan, obstruct airflow, change PWM/fan policy, inject faults, alter thresholds or power-cycle the chassis. Those operations are outside this passive row and can rapidly reduce thermal margin.
Use secret-safe protected access, complete output and no automatic retry; do not expose `-P`, assume cipher 17, use the first 100 SDR lines as coverage or execute the inaccessible Script.
agent_execution_scope: Validate canonical N, the fan/module/rotor/controller/zone map, discrete-state specification, supported protected client and Script/reference revision; build the complete expected channel set.
Read every exact STATUS_FAN record with stable SDR identity, raw state/masks, interpreted state, applicable threshold fields and timestamp; capture its exact Dashboard and Server Health row.
Record BMC polling time, current fan mode, associated RPM/tach values only as corroboration, and UI propagation delay; disposition optional/unfitted channels explicitly.
Return complete raw/redacted evidence without log clear, physical service, PWM/policy/fault/threshold/power mutation, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve N and the one-to-one channel-to-module/rotor/controller/zone map without borrowing the unresolved 16-fan scope from Wistron-BMC-00088-V004.
Provide discrete state/event mask/latch/freshness definitions, optional-position and redundancy rules, and clarify which threshold fields are applicable; approve tool or Project Override.
Review every required channel and issue the formal verdict without substituting RPM, temperature or unexecuted removal behavior for passive status display.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit because `1~N` is a symbolic scope, not an IPMI wildcard, and N has not been established. One lookup plus a truncated fallback cannot prove all discrete status channels; the command also exposes credentials and assumes a cipher suite.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover the full approved fan population and SDR inventory, query each exact status record through protected read-only access, decode its event state from the vendor definition and correlate all unchanged UI rows.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: STATUS_FAN 1~N, both UI paths, source readability/specification Criteria, generic clear wording, Script, DeepSeek command and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review resolves but does not overwrite N or add a fan fault.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Generate an expected fan-status set from approved platform inventory, then enumerate each exact SDR/API record and compare raw discrete bits, decoded state and timestamp with both UI locations and applicable status rules.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact chassis fan-board, module/rotor population and BMC monitoring implementation documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/fan-board, BMC/SDR/WebUI, fan-controller firmware, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform thermal/fan topology and redundancy specification, BMC SDR/event-state definition, fan-controller documentation and WebUI schema.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces symbolic N with an inventory-backed complete channel set and separates discrete status from RPM/temperature/threshold fields while preserving passive UI coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Passive normal-state display does not validate removal/insertion, stalled-rotor injection, redundancy transitions, fan-control response, thermal behavior, SEL generation or recovery.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Canonical N/topology, discrete-state map, applicability/freshness rules and validated collection interface.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: One module may expose multiple rotors or composite status, optional positions may be absent by design, and UI state can lag the raw BMC poll.

project_override_considerations: A Project-approved Redfish/OEM interface may replace or corroborate ipmitool only when the original method, replacement reason and engineer approval are recorded and equivalent identity, raw/decoded state, applicable thresholds, status and freshness are proven for the entire discovered N. RPM or thermal values alone are not equivalent status coverage.
expected_evidence: Chassis/fan-board/BMC identity and approved fitted fan-module/rotor inventory establishing N
Complete per-channel physical slot/module/rotor/controller/header/zone/redundancy plus SDR/API/UI identity matrix
Separate full raw discrete state, assertion/deassertion masks, decoded state, applicable/not-applicable threshold fields and synchronized timestamp for every channel
Redacted Dashboard and Server Health rows, recorded fan policy/polling/UI propagation and corroborating RPM only where mapped
Explicit optional/unfitted/absent/degraded/failed/unavailable/stale disposition, protected tool provenance, preserved logs, no-fault/no-fan-change/no-retry proof and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Within this row, Items, passive WebUI Procedure and Criteria consistently request fan status presentation. N is unresolved but can be supplied by Project inventory; the `1~N` versus `1~16` and temperature-status contradictions belong to the separate dynamic case and are not present here.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The passive all-installed-fan status objective is identifiable. Canonical inventory and the vendor discrete-state definition can resolve N and acceptance without a hardware fault, so Project readiness remains pending but the review is not permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes unsupported YES to PACKAGE and replaces a literal symbolic lookup with complete inventory-driven per-channel reads.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on classification and adds rotor-versus-module identity, discrete event masks, applicable-field handling, UI propagation and isolation from the pending dynamic fan decision.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence review with complete topology, state-decoding and raw/UI/freshness evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Preserves the separate engineer decision for physical fan-removal scope and does not credit RPM/thermal or fault behavior here.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact passive source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an invalid `1~N` lookup, assumed 16-fan population, rotor/module counting error or RPM/temperature evidence from being reported as complete status coverage, while preventing unsafe fan fault stimulation.
independent_technical_reasoning: Fan status is commonly a discrete or composite event record, not a numeric sensor with ordinary thresholds. Completeness depends on the chassis population model and whether modules expose one or multiple rotors. Therefore N must come from approved inventory, each state must be decoded from its event definition, and normal passive display cannot prove the separate physical-removal behavior.
